740720102.text: You bet we are! Have you found anything new in the meantime?

740720103.text: Mr. Caterpillar and I have been doing some research...

740720105.text: We've discovered that Seymour doesn't, in fact, have an "Annihilation mode."

740720106.text: Following data fragment sorting, this phrase was found to have been derived from the novel "Prisoner Six: Overrun."

740720107.text: In that book, the world organization launched a mass annihilation agent to hunt a chimera down...

740720108.text: Wait, that stuff's not important at all!

740720109.text: Apart from using our free time to go out and investigate, we've also read through the books collected here one more time.

740720110.text: We couldn't make heads or tails of them at first, and even now... Well, they certainly are well-written.

740720111.text: I don't know whose handwriting it is, or what scribe or copyist was hired, but their penmanship is clear and clearly beautiful — a master of calligraphy if I ever saw one.

740720112.text: Wait, so you were talking about the handwriting!

740720113.text: Ugh, Paimon's got a bad feeling about this already — did you not find anything during this time, then?

740720114.text: Heh, alright, sorry. I shan't jest any further.

740720115.text: As you know, we told you all that we found the last time without holding anything back.

740720116.text: However, I fear that this time, there are some clues hidden in details that we must rely on chance to reveal.

740720119.text: Indeed. For example, if no further revelations concerning a murder emerge, then the blood on a painting will always remain a red smear.

740720120.text: Then what would this "chance" be, Caterpillar?

740720121.text: Well... Why don't we do a quick recap of everything we've discovered?

740720122.text: Let's make some deductions regarding what happened in the past — that might give us the opportunity to fill in some gaps that can help us support or refute our views.

740720123.text: That's a good idea. I've always felt like there's so much about this that's familiar... but I can't recall anything about it.

740720124.text: Negative. I can give a continuous account of the resources that I have sorted—

740720125.text: Ugh, silly dog. Didn't you only recover your creator's name after talking to us about the matter?

740720126.text: *mechanical noises* ...Negative. I merely matched similar sounds during said interaction. There was no data loss involved.

740720127.text: However, I must append that I, too, find that keyword searches make searching for entries more efficient.

740720128.text: So, what do we want to discuss?

740720129.text: Well, for a bit of a warmup, or a teaser, if you would—

740720130.text: You may be referring to a "heater."

740720131.text: Yes, that's exactly what I mean — so, let's start off our deductions with something simple.

740720132.text: What is the "Mary-Ann" in the Annapausis, exactly?

740720134.text: That "Mary-Ann" holds the greatest secret of all — I'm sure you can see that too.

740720135.text: Let's get ourselves some armchairs, maybe crack open a few beers... Oh, wait, you can't drink yet.

740720136.text: Anyway, let us help you sort our findings out.

740720137.text: I'll start first. Well, the name "Mary-Ann" itself certainly is familiar to me.

740720138.text: The name of the person I was meant to protect is "Mary-Ann," yes, but I have no data regarding the identity of the one who resides within the Annapausis.

740720139.text: We are missing context — I can only conclude, based on a human's unmodified lifespan, that they are not the same person.

740720140.text: That would seem to be the case, huh? It's been a few hundred years, after all.

740720141.text: Well, as for Paimon... She ate Chicken-Mushroom Skewer this morning...?

740720142.text: Well, guess it's my turn — you mentioned before that you encountered Oceanid creatures that had a great deal of character... One might say "personality," even.

740720143.text: The precondition for such creatures and their characters is the same — that an intelligent Oceanid has already understood their original forms beforehand.

740720144.text: So, were you the one who willed those creatures into being, Ann?

740720145.text: Uh, don't you think that's kinda weird — y'know, summoning familiar friends to play house with you for who knows how long and stuff?

740720146.text: Well, I didn't do that! I actually had to get to know Petit Chou, Al, and the others first.

740720147.text: Well, then. In that case, let's see what we can deduce from the things we already know.

740720202.text: So, regarding Alain's younger sister <color=#00E1FFFF>Mary-Ann</color>, the Annapausis's <color=#00E1FFFF>"Mary-Ann"</color>, the Red Empress <color=#00E1FFFF>Lyris</color>, and the <color=#00E1FFFF>Ann</color> who's with us...

740720203.text: What will our conclusion be? How will we sustain it, and how shall we refute it?

740720205.text: Is there anything else you feel we should add?

740720206.text: As I mentioned before, Mary-Ann is not only the Princess in Ann's story, but she is also the person I must protect.

740720207.text: She is the younger sister of Alain Guillotin, the one who designed me, 4ACV07.

740720208.text: #As for matters concerning me, I suppose you already know all about them, Knight {NICKNAME}.

740720209.text: Speaking of which, didn't we also hear all sorts of stuff while we were in Elynas?

740720210.text: Seymour was also damaged during that time...

740720211.text: How did it go? Did you think of anything?

740720301.text: So, could you tell us what you heard?

740720302.text: Perhaps a hilichurl might hear something that humans and Oceanids will not, just as how dogs and humans differ in that regard.

740720303.text: I must correct your statement. My auditory components can indeed pick up higher and lower frequencies as compared to humans. However, I am not a dog. Moreover, a dog's low-frequency hearing is similar to that of a human.

740720304.text: Is that so? Well, I was talking about real dogs, not you, 4ACV07.

740720306.text: #That said, I didn't think you would hear it too, Knight {NICKNAME}. I wonder if we'd heard the same thing.

740720308.text: "They won't come back, no matter how long I wait..."

740720309.text: Looks like we heard the same thing. I suspect that this was the inner voice of "Mary-Ann."

740720310.text: #Did she say anything else? I'm not trying to invade anyone's privacy or anything. I just think that we're onto something here with you mentioning these words, {NICKNAME}.

740720311.text: Let me think... After that, I also heard something like "I prefer the story of the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team sitting down happily for tea time after their adventure has ended."

740720313.text: "I don't want to hear your stories... I prefer my version."

740720314.text: #...Have you noticed something off about this, {NICKNAME}?

740720316.text: Let's think our own thoughts through first. Perhaps we really might be able to come to some conclusion.

740720401.text: We're back again. This time, I must... Mary-Ann...

740720403.text: In truth, I must confess to being somewhat jealous of you.

740720405.text: You still hold out hope of recovering your past. I've... been searching for centuries, but I haven't found a thing.

740720406.text: So please, do your best for this old caterpillar's part as well, alright? Figure your past out, and come to accept your present self.

740721501.text: That's enough for now. More than enough for a warm-up.

740721502.text: Correct. The oddities in Annapausis all point to the <color=#00E1FFFF>powers of the Oceanids</color>.

740721503.text: But this is not Miss Ann's doing. All of this together means...

740721505.text: That is what I suspect. <color=#00E1FFFF>An Oceanid with whom Mary-Ann has a close relationship</color>.

740721506.text: Or perhaps, she could even be... the princess herself.

740721507.text: Do you mean to say that <color=#00E1FFFF>"Mary-Ann" may, in fact, be Princess Lyris</color>?

740721508.text: Yes, Lyris. The Red Empress of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo from back then, the Red Empress who loves to take heads.

740721510.text: I seem to have a vague recollection of something like that.

740721512.text: But it's not a story about Lyris. Rather, it's a fairytale about someone named Mary-Ann.

740721513.text: Yes. The taking heads thing is just a metaphor. <color=#00E1FFFF>Lyris is made of pure water and so has the ability to dissolve and extract people's wills</color>.

740721514.text: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo used her to extract the ego and become holy.

740721515.text: Searching for the keyword "Lyris" has yielded relevant information in my indices.

740721516.text: Talking of the Red Empress has reminded me of a few things about Mary-Ann.

740721517.text: Mull that over a while first, then speak to Miss Ann and Seymour.

740721518.text: See if the conclusion you reach awakens any new memories.

740722104.text: It's familiar to me because it's from a children's story. The same one that the "Red Empress" comes from.

740722105.text: The female lead, Liddell, was mistaken for Mary-Ann, the servant. And Mary-Ann never appeared throughout the entire story.

740722106.text: Maybe <color=#00E1FFFF>"Mary-Ann" never really existed... except as a figment in someone's dreams</color>.

740722107.text: How do you know about this story, Ann?

740722108.text: And isn't that a good question? How do I know about it?

740722109.text: The memory feels more vivid than those I have of the story of the evil dragon, Narcissus.

subQuests.subQuestName: Collect more leads and gather your thoughts

740722201.text: Shall I summarize the entries regarding Lyris I possess for you two?

740722204.text: Omitting the standard citation format. Reconstructing output to match format "report to superiors"...

740722205.text: Lyris is a registered Oceanid. She is not eligible to be stationed in the waters outside Fontaine and has become...

740722206.text: A special source of information for the nation. She was appointed as the director of an orphanage to symbolize the love and affection of the previous Hydro Archon.

740722207.text: The orphanage's affairs were mainly managed by its human vice director.

740722208.text: An orphanage director... Then how is she connected to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo?

740722209.text: As Director, Lyris was very affectionate towards the children and quite devoted to them, but <color=#00E1FFFF>her intelligence among Oceanids was below average</color>.

740722210.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>She wasn't very good at working out the cause and effect of things, nor could she even count</color>. As a result, she was not qualified to perform covert investigations.

740722211.text: Aww, sounds kinda like a big ol' cat mom who can't count!

740722212.text: Y'know, because cats can't count, so they pick up their kittens one by one, and keep going back until they see there aren't any kittens left!

740722213.text: Later, the orphanage was destroyed during the calamity, and official records of her stop there.

740722214.text: They say she failed to understand the link between the disaster, the orphans fleeing, and her own conduct, and so she wanders the ruins, drowning in guilt and expectation.

740722215.text: I have an underwater locomotion module. Once, Mary-Ann and I... dove down to the ruins of the orphanage, whose coordinates were the same as those of Annapausis.

740722216.text: There, we found an Oceanid swimming sadly in circles...

740722217.text: When she next appeared in the records, she was a core member of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo and the subject of a high-priority arrest warrant.

740722218.text: Oh, but she doesn't seem like a bad person.

740722219.text: Considering that she may be connected to Ann, she must've been tricked.

740722220.text: Ah, yes. There's another important piece of information worth noting. The orphanage's name was—

740722223.text: These are all Marechaussee Phantom files that Mr. Alain Guillotin recorded for testing light sensitivity while designing me. The output is via my image-to-text-to-speech module.

740722224.text: According to eyewitness testimony regarding who I suspect to be Lyris, there shouldn't be any problems.

740722225.text: And you may have heard of this elsewhere, but it's worth mentioning again:

740722226.text: Alain and Mary-Ann were orphans in the care of the Narzissenkreuz Institute before the Marechaussee Hunter, Emanuel Guillotin, took them in.

740722301.text: Paimon feels like you've changed a lot since we met in the Fortress of Meropide, Caterpillar...

740722302.text: Would a five-year-old child and a fifteen-year-old teenager be the same? Perhaps returning here simply reminds me of the past, and of who I used to be.

740722303.text: Time is frozen in the Fortress. Being locked up there for a day, or a hundred years... I'm afraid it made no difference to me.

740722304.text: Lanoire is what made time flow for me. Watching her grow reminded me that time still passes, and life is still being born, shining brilliantly, and then being extinguished.

740722305.text: And so I changed as well. That said, my past self — the person I was before I met her — would certainly be more helpful to Ann and Seymour in our current situation.

740722307.text: Haha! Don't be like that, Paimon! Just think about it — making up stories for Lanoire was nothing more than putting such ways of thinking to good use.

740722308.text: #Regardless, it has nothing to do with the current situation. You look like you still have questions, {NICKNAME}.

740722309.text: Since we have our own suspicions about Ann and Lyris's relationship, we have topics of discussion that can be used to refute or sustain those conjectures.

740722311.text: I'm sure you have friends more knowledgeable than I am regarding that. Perhaps you can even find scholars of natural philosophy who have dedicated research to the question.

740722312.text: Or you could have asked the Oceanids you know personally... but you asked me.

740722313.text: Of course, I know what you mean. So this is your speculation? I see.

740722315.text: #When we exchanged information earlier, {NICKNAME} mentioned that <color=#00E1FFFF>Ann is the person in "Mary-Ann's" dream</color>.

740722316.text: Or perhaps, she might be a manifestation made by "Mary-Ann" — an Oceanid-Oceanid.

740722317.text: Oceanid-Oceanid? Why the repetition? ...Are you just trying to make it sound cuter?

740722318.text: Apologies, perhaps my description was ill-done. Still, can an Oceanid create an Oceanid-creature version of an Oceanid?

740722319.text: Wow, that's deep! That's like asking if hard candies can be used as the filler for another hard candy.

740722320.text: So, what would you say to that? This question's really interesting, but Paimon's already hungry for answers!

740722323.text: Still, you may not realize just how deep this rabbit hole goes, so let me explain.

740722325.text: You might be confused as to why there are Oceanid creatures with personalities in the Annapausis.

740722326.text: If Oceanids can create Oceanid creatures, then can they create Oceanid-Humans or Oceanid-Oceanids?

740722327.text: Convention dictates that it's rare for Oceanids to be able to mimic a human, unless the human drowns in their arms, or the Oceanid has spent extensive time with the person and knows everything about them.

740722328.text: And the Oceanid in question must also have tremendous wisdom and compassion. I'm afraid perhaps only one as powerful as Rhodeia could do it.

740722329.text: Wow, so that means Idyia must be incredibly strong...

740722330.text: So it's rare to mimic humans, but not impossible. Now, creating another Oceanid... That's different.

740722331.text: Creating humans using human knowledge can only be achieved by gods, and the same applies to Oceanids creating Oceanids. It usually should be impossible — in this world, at least.

740722332.text: Unless... Unless this human or Oceanid has already placed themselves above their own kind, and attempted such insanity.

740722333.text: You mean... They thought they had become a god?

740722334.text: That's right. Followers blindly believe in their leaders, who in turn blindly believe in themselves, giving rise to delirium and delusions.

740722335.text: "I can do what a god can do. Their deeds are not that great, after all."

740722336.text: A powerful belief is also a powerful will, and magic is a skill that molds reality to your will.

740724101.text: I am very sorry. I may be unable to offer any logical support at this time.

740724102.text: My listening equipment cannot hear inner voices.

740724103.text: Don't worry, you've helped plenty already.

740724104.text: Could you tell me your assessment? Is the Mary-Ann from Annapausis the person I am meant to protect or not?

740724106.text: I am willing to believe your judgment, even if that means I have to update my data.

740724107.text: According to my records, Mary-Ann Guillotin never exhibited the behavior of waiting for others to come back after the Narzissenkreuz Institute was destroyed.

740724108.text: That means she must have returned to the ruins here after being adopted, living there for a while. But there is no possible timeframe that meets these requirements.

740724112.text: "I prefer the story of the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team sitting down happily for tea time after their adventure has ended."

740724113.text: It seems that she, too, was an orphan from the Narzissenkreuz Institute, but other relevant information cannot be matched to her.

740721602.text: That makes her our prime suspect, then.

740721603.text: To be honest, were you using the process of elimination, you actually already guessed as much long ago.

740721604.text: I didn't want to disrespect Ann, though.

740721605.text: You're right. But you do already have a version of the story in your heart — your own interpretation, yes?

740721606.text: If that's the case, then we should go find that "Mary-Ann," and see for ourselves.

740721607.text: Please permit me to change the topic for a moment.

740721608.text: Does this mean that I shall no longer be able to fulfill my orders to protect Mary-Ann?

740721609.text: We've worked out this much, and that's the only bit you care about?

740721610.text: Hmm, it may be cruel, but from the moment we discovered that the Guillotin siblings were from centuries ago, it was probably inevitable...

740721611.text: Correction. So, the conclusion would be that it was my incompetence that exposed Mary-Ann to danger?

740721612.text: Do not blame yourself. You have fought to the point of destruction. You have done your part.

740721613.text: There's no need to be so pessimistic either. Though that is an odd thing to say to a machine.

740721614.text: Yeah. It's like pouring Fonta into a sink and then saying "Sink, you'll get fat if you keep drinking like this!"

740721616.text: I can't believe you remember that...

740721617.text: What is it, Mr. Caterpillar? Why use my official designation?

740721618.text: We may not have reached any conclusions. But we now know what to do next.

740721619.text: Look. There is a Mary-Ann in Annapausis too, and she also has close links to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

740721620.text: My long-term memory module confirms this.

740721621.text: As such, there's no need to restore your logic module to factory settings yet. Let's take a step back.

740721622.text: We can still go and find this Mary-Ann.

740721624.text: Thank you for your logical troubleshooting and... emotional adaptive maintenance.

740721625.text: I think... what you said makes sense. It is not yet time to admit defeat and restore myself to my initial settings in order to take on a new mission.

740721626.text: Yeah! That's right, you silly doggy!

740721627.text: Let's leave things here for a while, then. Once you are ready, we can continue.

740721628.text: Hmm. Why don't we go find this Mary-Ann?

740721629.text: Let's solve that mystery before tackling the Narzissenkreuz Ordo issue.

740721631.text: Mmhmm. I'd really like to figure that one out too. After all, it might explain where I come from.

740721632.text: My logic module agrees that this is the correct course of action.

740721634.text: Hmm? I gather that some things happened over there, then?

740721635.text: #Oh, we just ran into "immunity"-related issues often due to Knight {NICKNAME}'s Hydro resonance, that's all.

740721636.text: Paimon feels like some extraordinary instinct awakened in you after you met Seymour, Ann...

740721637.text: Is it time to review responsibilities and apportion blame? I do not think I should be held accountable, for I can only override my protective prerogative in moments of great danger.

740721638.text: #Don't worry, Knight {NICKNAME}. We'll make "Mary-Ann" tell us everything this time.

740722401.text: Whoa! What are these guys doing here again?

740722403.text: #Hohoho! Yes, it is us. And you are... Knight {NICKNAME} and Paimon?

740722404.text: It's really good to see you. So good that I can't control myself anymore. Please dodge to the best of your ability.

740722405.text: She asked us to send you a message. Now let me take out her handwritten letter with my hands, which are much like yours, yellow and white ones. Ahem—

740722406.text: "I don't want to hear your stories... I prefer my version."

740722602.text: There are four Seals in total. If my hypothesis is correct, then they should be at these locations, respectively...

740722604.text: We've been to some of them before during our adventures.

740722605.text: I see. And did you find anything there?

740722607.text: ...I see. This proves two things. Firstly, my hypothesis is accurate.

740722609.text: Secondly, the situation is grim. We need to get moving and see if we still have a chance to turn things around.

subQuests.subQuestName: Stop Al and Jak, who have lost control

740722702.text: There are four Seals in total. If my hypothesis is correct, then they should be at these locations, respectively...

740722704.text: We've been to them during our adventures.

740722705.text: Well, to be precise, we've been to three out of the four locations.

740722706.text: I see. And did you find anything there?

740722708.text: ...I see. This proves two things. Firstly, my hypothesis is accurate.

740722710.text: The situation is grim. We must hurry to the fourth location.

740720501.text: Huh. The bubble that was here before is gone, too.

740720502.text: Well, it was Princess Lyris's magic... That's just how the story goes.

740720503.text: Let me think of a way.

740720505.text: A temporary optical sensor shutdown? Understood. They will be reactivated on your command.

740720506.text: Wait, why do we have to do that?

740720507.text: The essence of a mime is pretense — the charade that something is still here.

740720508.text: And belief is the heart of magic, the faith that there is meaning here... so, let's close our eyes.

740720509.text: So, Ann, begin imagining what it would look like if that bubble was still here.

740720510.text: You close your eyes, and feel some sort of fluctuation...

740720511.text: "I prefer the story of the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team sitting down happily for tea time after their adventure has ended."

740720513.text: The Ordo called this step, the process of imagining something in such detail, "imaging."

740720514.text: Let's go over and have a look.

740722901.text: Tell me about what happened previously.

740722902.text: Hmm. You didn't go ahead and save the world while we split up to investigate, now did you?

740722903.text: A lot has happened indeed. It's no wonder you've forgotten what we went through together.

740722904.text: I jest, of course. Maybe you're just tired, and it's eluding you for now.

740722905.text: To put it simply, we met in the Fortress of Meropide, and you helped me rescue Lanoire.

740722906.text: And now, it's my turn to help you.

740720601.text: Eh? It's the entrance that's disappeared this time?

740720602.text: Ann, do you know to make the portal... Uh, can you do your "imaging" thing on it?

740720603.text: Alright. Let me give it a try.

740720604.text: You close your eyes, and a lonesome silence comes over you...

740720605.text: "But everyone's left. They won't come back, no matter how long I wait..."

740720608.text: How are we supposed to see Mary-Ann, then?

740720609.text: I suspect that this is because the portal has lost meaning, and thus cannot be recreated.

740720611.text: From what you told me before, the entrance that was once placed here led to a story that had yet to be written.

740720612.text: Now that she has said everything she wanted to, the story no longer has any meaning. Mary-Ann is rejecting our answer, and that is why the way in is shut.

740720613.text: Does... Does this mean we're going to return empty-handed?

740720615.text: I wouldn't say we're completely out of luck.

740720616.text: #Did you notice something we didn't then, Knight {NICKNAME}?

740720617.text: I heard something while Ann was "imaging."

740720618.text: I did hear something then... So you can hear it too?

740720619.text: Would that be Mary-Ann's real thoughts?

740720621.text: Ah, hmm, might be best not to discuss personal secrets here — the walls might have ears and all. Let's head back before talking about this.

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to Caterpillar when you're ready

740722001.text: We've put the pieces of the case that were floating all over the algae sea back together.

740722002.text: It's just an empty box even after being put together, but we've finally figured out...

740722003.text: What the lost pearl should look like.

740722004.text: Uhm, what are you trying to say, Caterpillar?

740722005.text: Wait. Don't give Paimon any hints. She's gonna figure this out on her own!

740722006.text: We pieced together a good guess from the clues, but the truth is... still unproven?

740722007.text: Of course. My speech analysis module has determined that Miss Paimon is correct.

740722008.text: Actually, I meant that we may never know the truth. But I'm afraid we have no choice but to accept this conjecture.

740722009.text: #So, Knight {NICKNAME}, is this the secret of my birth?

740722010.text: It's... I'm afraid I can't... accept something like this right away...

740722011.text: I understand, Ms. Ann. It's a shocking fact, and it'll require you to accept yourself again.

740722012.text: But I don't think it should be that difficult to do so. After all, knowing your past does not require abandoning everything about the present.

740722013.text: I do not understand the specific context of this discussion. But I would like to add that I do not believe I am different from how I was before suffering disk damage.

740722014.text: Even though you insist on addressing me as a silly dog, my identification number is still 4ACV07.

740722015.text: #Come on, it's not that serious! I promised Knight {NICKNAME} that I would accept this conclusion, as long as it's reasonable.

740722016.text: Then I have a suggestion, one that will resolve Miss Ann's quandary and put a stop to Narzissenkreuz's plans.

740722018.text: Narzissen... Oh! Paimon remembers now! You mentioned him before, Caterpillar. Just who is he, huh?

740722019.text: Well... Simply put, the leader of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

740722020.text: Whoa! Sounds like he's got an impressive resume! But isn't the Narzissenkreuz Ordo always up to no good? Wouldn't that make him the nastiest of the lot?

740722021.text: Of course. During my time with my master, creator, and the other Marechaussee Hunters, we devoted most of our time to hunting the Ordo down.

740722022.text: As I said before, the goal of the Elynas operation was to capture or eliminate Narzissenkreuz as well. However, my memory does not contain any intelligence regarding his involvement.

740722023.text: That's a given. Looking back at it now, he was merely using us as bait. And I wasn't the only one... It was the same for Jakob, Lyris, and many others in the Ordo.

740722024.text: I'm afraid the Elynas operation was probably never more than a red herring with the goal of leading you and Guillotin away to buy him more time to execute his true plans.

740722025.text: Remember the Doomsday Clock I mentioned?

740722026.text: It's what the Ordo considers the countdown to the apocalypse, right?

740722027.text: To be more precise, it's the apocalypse as calculated by the world-formula. This planet itself should survive just fine, though...

740722028.text: "The beast of the stars shall drink the amniotic fluid of the world dry. A hundred years more, and all surface life shall be wiped away."

740722029.text: Once life on the surface is wiped out, only that which is underwater will remain. Can a planet full of fish eventually rise up to the ocean of stars?

740722030.text: The thought of all terrestrial life going extinct is pretty spooky, but when you say things like that, it does give things a romantic ring...

740722031.text: It's the heading of a Yae Publishing House novel from a few years back. Mamere brought it back to the village to learn how to paint.

740722033.text: Anyways, for myself and the others gathered here, though the Narzissenkreuz Ordo is the source of all our troubles...

740722034.text: Its objective and Narzissenkreuz's great purpose are actually completely selfless.

740722035.text: He only took the actions he did because he calculated the coming of the apocalypse. He wishes to save the world.

740722036.text: So is the world really on the verge of destruction?

740722037.text: I believe this to be a pathological delusion caused by paranoia.

740722038.text: Were the apocalypse real... would you be able to forgive Narzissenkreuz?

740722039.text: No. It's a bit too early to consider such things. You have yet to understand what happened to you, Ann.

740722040.text: And as for you, Seymour, your hostility is a result of your programming and the duties it imposes.

740722041.text: I suppose we must find the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz.

740722043.text: I'm talking about the real one, of course... as much as it may be quite strange to say that the ceremonial sword of a magic society is real.

740722044.text: Not only will it help us stop Narzissenkreuz's plans, but its unique powers may be able to undo the merging of wills.

740722045.text: We should be able to separate Lyris and Mary-Ann. And then, Miss Ann, you can defeat the evil dragon, Narcissus, and rescue Princess Lyris.

740722048.text: That's the spirit. It might take some time to explain, so let's move out first and I'll explain when we get there.

740720701.text: Atmospheric visibility is acceptable today... Enough that you can see that tower over there, yes?

740720704.text: That building was once known to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo as the "Tower of Ipsissimus," but we would later call it the "Tower of Gestalt."

740720705.text: It was named for the idea that things that have been separated need to be combined to display their original, complete form.

740720706.text: But I suppose I might be speaking in reverse. The heart was complete to begin with — and the mistake was to divide it up for separate study.

740720707.text: Uh, Paimon didn't get a thing you said.

740720708.text: It's fine, don't worry about it. Plays on words are also a trick that mysterious organizations enjoy pulling. What matters is what we must do next.

740720709.text: Some of the vocabulary you used is missing from my semantic indexes, so I could not properly parse your meaning.

740720710.text: But I understood the last sentence. Please tell me what I should do.

740720711.text: While investigating alone, I found a map of the Seal of Chymical Marriage. You could say that I've found four seals.

740720712.text: And this tower is one of the locations?

740720713.text: That's not the place we need to go. That said, though, who can be sure? Perhaps our destinies will yet take us there in the future.

740720714.text: Either way, we need to use the position of the tower to locate the other four places. That's why we've come here first.

740720715.text: So what are those four seals for?

740720716.text: That said, we've discovered from experience that it's usually best practice to just break the seals and give whatever ringleader we find a good walloping.

740720717.text: As for me, I'd like to restore the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz.

740723202.text: Anyway, assuming I looked at the map from the right angle, we will find the entrance to one of the Seals nearby.

740720801.text: Then we ended up at the top of that Tower of Gestalt place.

740720802.text: We're separated from Caterpillar, Ann, and Seymour...

740720803.text: What should we do? It looks like there are traps waiting down below.

740720806.text: C'mon, you should have at least a little sense of urgency!

740720807.text: Paimon knows you're a good fighter, but Paimon's worried about the others.

740720808.text: But our only choice is to keep going... Oh, is that the entrance?

740720809.text: If there's any traps, just smash 'em!

740720902.text: What took you so long? I've even had time to finish the anti-rust treatment and oil it up.

740720905.text: ...I've told you, just call me Jakob.

740720906.text: How did you set up this trap?

740720907.text: I believe the "Persona" section to be the most important, for there lies the persona excised by Master Narzissenkreuz himself.

740720908.text: Only a drop of water from an Oceanid can open it. I can't allow it to be taken by just any ignorant adventurer.

740720909.text: So I set a trap before activating the Orthant and sealed the space off.

740720911.text: Why shouldn't I be here? This is a Narzissenkreuz Ordo base. Is there something wrong with returning to my own base?

740720912.text: You're the ones who are trespassing. Don't you feel even a twinge of guilt for breaking the law?

740720913.text: "This was once the realm of a god. Now, a pheasant sits upon the throne." Just like the world today.

740720914.text: As compensation, give me the rest of your paints and the "Persona" I need.

740720916.text: Even now, at a time like this... Just what are you so hung up on?

740720917.text: The countdown to the world's end has started. I must forge the Holy Blade and place it in my Master's hand.

740720919.text: Indeed. According to his world-formula, the second deluge is looming before us. When it comes, only he will be able to save the world.

740720920.text: Only by forging the Holy Blade can he continue his unfinished work, gathering the wills of everyone in Fontaine, the continent, and even the entire planet unto himself.

740720921.text: As the primordial sea returns once more, and as the devourer of all darkens the sky, only he who is whole unto himself may survive.

740720922.text: Only then will all of our souls — nay, all of humanity's souls — be spared from destruction. We will welcome a new dawn in the tranquil sea of innocence he grants us.

740720923.text: So this is your big plan to save the world?

740720924.text: It sounds like you're just bundling everyone's consciousness together without consent.

740720925.text: And what would you know of anything? Only Master Narzissenkreuz's new body will survive the coming of the second deluge.

740720926.text: Even if all other life disappears into the sea, he will survive alone. He will remember all those lives that were lost.

740720927.text: He recognizes the value and equality of all life — a selflessness that shall not be besmirched by ones such as you.

740720929.text: In the deepest depths beneath us. When the thugs and dogs of Fontaine surrounded us and attempted to wipe us out, he descended alone into the abyss below.

740720930.text: But he must still be alive, and the time for his return is nigh.

740720931.text: Quickly, give me what you have on you. Then I will have all the Orthants, and you may leave.

740720932.text: How about this? I will trade you this rust treatment and oil. Think of it as a gift for that foolish dog.

740720933.text: In the dawn of the new world, it is unlikely there will be a place for it or Guillotin's fantasies.

740720934.text: I refuse. The world is not as weak as you think.

740720936.text: Truly, there is no reaching your exalted heights.

740720938.text: Who would have thought he would become the hero, while the real evil dragons would come at us, one after another.

740720940.text: What the heck are you talking about?

740720941.text: The time has come. A century ago, the prophecy predicted all. He will return.

740720942.text: If you will not give me what I need willingly, I will take it myself.

740723834.text: That's right. Followers blindly believe in their leaders, who in turn blindly believe in themselves, giving rise to delirium and delusions.

740724302.text: Is there anything else you want to say?
